description: The last leader of the Soviet Union, Gorbachev launched perestroika and glasnost, liberalizing the economy and the press, reduced the nuclear arsenal with the West, and allowed the fall of the Berlin Wall, precipitating the collapse of the communist bloc.

name: Arthur Schopenhauer
description: A German philosopher, Schopenhauer saw the blind Will as the irrational essence of reality, a source of perpetual suffering, and advocated compassion, art and ascetic renunciation as the only relief, in a pessimism skeptical of all Enlightenment and political optimism.

name: Max Weber
description: A German sociologist and founder of modern sociology, Weber analyzed rational-legal bureaucracy, distinguished types of legitimate authority, and linked the Protestant ethic to the spirit of capitalism, without prescribing a political program of his own.

name: Jiang Zemin
description: Chinese Communist Party general secretary from 1989 to 2002, Jiang preserved the party monopoly after Tiananmen, suppressed Falun Gong and promoted the Three Represents, WTO accession and reform of state-owned enterprises.

name: Hu Jintao
description: Chinese Communist Party general secretary from 2002 to 2012, Hu formulated the Harmonious Society and Scientific Development, sustained growth with higher social spending and tightened digital censorship and repression in Tibet and Xinjiang.

name: Tony Blair
description: British prime minister from 1997 to 2007, Blair took New Labour to the Third Way, with markets, investment in education and tough sentencing, backed the invasion of Iraq and now champions digital ID and AI in government.

name: Geraldo Alckmin
description: Four-time governor of São Paulo for the center-right PSDB, with concessions, PPPs and isolation of prison gang leaders, Alckmin moved to the PSB and is Lula's vice president and industry minister, backing reindustrialization and the Mercosur-EU deal and opposing abortion.

name: J. R. R. Tolkien
description: Oxford philologist and author of The Lord of the Rings, Tolkien was a devout Catholic who distrusted the modern state and industrialization, said he leaned toward anarchy or unconstitutional monarchy and idealized the rural life of the Shire.

name: Pope Leo XIII
description: Pope from 1878 to 1903, Leo XIII founded Catholic social teaching with the encyclical Rerum Novarum, defending a just wage, workers' associations and private property against socialism and liberalism, and revived Thomism.

name: Baron of Rio Branco
description: Foreign minister from 1902 to 1912, the Baron of Rio Branco settled Brazil's borders through arbitration and negotiation, as in Acre and Misiones, drew the country closer to the United States and made law and diplomacy the basis of foreign policy.

name: Rui Barbosa
description: Jurist and senator, Rui Barbosa drafted Brazil's first republican constitution, championed federalism, habeas corpus and civil liberties, argued for the equality of nations at The Hague and led the Civilian Campaign against militarism.

name: Carlos Lacerda
description: Journalist and leader of the UDN party, Lacerda traded youthful communism for liberal anticommunism, helped topple Vargas and back the 1964 coup, governed Guanabara with major public works and favela removals and later founded the Broad Front.

name: Luís Carlos Prestes
description: Leader of the Prestes Column and for decades head of the Brazilian Communist Party, Prestes led the 1935 communist uprising, was jailed under the Estado Novo, elected senator in 1945 and followed the Soviet line until breaking with the party in 1980.

name: Mário Covas
description: Opposition leader stripped of his mandate by the dictatorship and founder of the PSDB, Covas called for a capitalism shock in the 1989 campaign and, as governor of São Paulo, pursued fiscal adjustment, privatizations and concessions with a social democratic, ethical message.

name: Baron of Mauá
description: Industrialist and banker of the Brazilian Empire, Mauá founded a shipyard, a foundry, Brazil's first railway and banks across the River Plate; a liberal critic of slavery, he clashed with the government's restrictive credit policy and went bankrupt in 1875.

name: Paulo Guedes
description: A Chicago-trained economist and Bolsonaro's economy minister, Guedes delivered pension reform and central bank autonomy, preached sweeping privatisations that never happened, and loosened the federal spending cap.

name: Guilherme Boulos
description: A founder of the Homeless Workers' Movement and the most-voted federal deputy for São Paulo in 2022, Boulos rose from housing and urban reform struggles to the left, joining the presidential cabinet in 2025.

name: Alexandre de Moraes
description: A supreme court justice and former São Paulo public security secretary, Moraes led the prosecution of the January 2023 coup attempt and of the former president convicted over it, becoming the right's main target.

name: Tarcísio de Freitas
description: A military engineer and Bolsonaro's infrastructure minister, Tarcísio has governed São Paulo since 2023 with concessions, privatisations and a technocratic managerial pitch, running for re-election in 2026.

name: João Doria
description: A businessman and broadcaster, Doria was mayor and governor of São Paulo, led the covid vaccination drive against the federal government and privatised state companies; now partyless, he backs a centrist path.

name: Eduardo Leite
description: Governor of Rio Grande do Sul, Leite privatised the state water and power utilities and reformed its pension system; the first Brazilian governor to come out as gay, he switched parties to run in 2026.

name: Fernando Haddad
description: An economist and former mayor of São Paulo, Haddad served as education and finance minister, passing a new fiscal framework and a landmark tax reform; he left the cabinet in 2026 to run for state governor.

name: Nero
description: The last Julio-Claudian emperor, Nero had his own mother Agrippina killed, persecuted Christians after the Great Fire of Rome in 64 AD, and grew ever more tyrannical and extravagant until his suicide in 68, ending the dynasty.

name: Christopher Columbus
description: A Genoese navigator sailing for the Catholic Monarchs, he reached the Americas in 1492 seeking a trade route to the Indies. As colonial governor, he enslaved indigenous people in pursuit of gold and was arrested and sent to Spain in chains for abuses of power.

name: William of Orange
description: A Lutheran-born noble who converted to Catholicism and later Calvinism, William led the Dutch Revolt against Philip II of Spain, championed relative religious tolerance, and was assassinated in 1584 by a Spanish agent, becoming the "father of the fatherland."

name: René Descartes
description: A French philosopher and mathematician, father of modern philosophy and creator of analytic geometry, Descartes formulated methodic doubt and mind-body dualism ("I think, therefore I am"). He lived in the tolerant Dutch Republic, avoiding conflict with the Church after Galileo.

name: Isaac Newton
description: An English physicist and mathematician, Newton founded classical mechanics and infinitesimal calculus in the "Principia Mathematica." He ran the Royal Society with an iron fist and, as Master of the Royal Mint, hunted counterfeiters to the gallows. A secret alchemist and anti-trinitarian.

name: Albert Einstein
description: A German-Swiss-American theoretical physicist, he created the theories of relativity and won the 1921 Nobel Prize. A Jewish refugee from Nazism in 1933, he was a pacifist, a declared socialist in "Why Socialism?," and an advocate of world government and civil rights.

name: Voltaire
description: A French Enlightenment writer and philosopher, he attacked religious fanaticism and the Church ("crush the infamous thing"), championed free speech and tolerance in the Calas affair, but favored enlightened monarchy over popular democracy. Deist, author of Candide.

name: Nikola Tesla
description: A Serbian-American inventor, pioneer of alternating current and induction motors, he rivaled Edison in the "war of currents." A visionary obsessed with wireless energy, he saw universal electrification as human liberation and preached world peace through technology.

name: Alan Turing
description: A British mathematician and logician, he cracked the Nazi Enigma code at Bletchley Park and laid the theoretical foundations of computing (Turing Machine, Turing Test). Prosecuted for homosexuality in 1952, chemically castrated, he died in 1954; posthumously pardoned in 2013.

name: Sérgio Moro
description: A former federal judge, Moro led Operation Car Wash (Lava Jato), Brazil's biggest corruption probe, targeting state oil giant Petrobras, then served as justice minister under Bolsonaro before resigning; now running for governor of Paraná in 2026.

name: Belisarius
description: Byzantium's most successful general under Justinian I, he reconquered Vandal North Africa and Ostrogothic Italy, and crushed the Nika riots (532) with a massacre at the Hippodrome. Loyal to the emperor even under suspicion and humiliation, he ran a rigidly disciplined army.

name: J. Robert Oppenheimer
description: American theoretical physicist who directed the Manhattan Project at Los Alamos, widely regarded as the father of the atomic bomb. After Hiroshima and Nagasaki, he advocated for civilian and international control of nuclear weapons and had his security clearance revoked during McCarthyism (1954).

name: Kim Kataguiri
description: Federal deputy for São Paulo, MBL co-founder, re-elected in 2026 for Mission. Combines free markets and administrative reform with tough-on-crime policy, tech-focused industrial policy and moderate social conservatism.

name: Pablo Marçal
description: Evangelical entrepreneur and influencer whose 2026 presidential registration was denied. He advocates an entrepreneurial society, privatization, digital technocratic management and a national crackdown on gangs, combining tax cuts with continued cash transfers.

name: Richard Rasmussen
description: Biologist and TV adventure host, he served as Bolsonaro’s tourism ambassador and ran for Congress in 2026. He champions wildlife breeders, Amazon smallholders and cattle grazing as fire prevention, criticizing environmental enforcement and NGOs.

name: Machado de Assis
description: Brazil's greatest writer and founder of the Brazilian Academy of Letters, he ironically portrayed the elite of the Second Empire. A civil servant, he was a moderate liberal, a discreet abolitionist and skeptical of religion and scientism.

name: Santos Dumont
description: Aviation pioneer who flew the 14-bis in Paris in 1906 and left his inventions in the public domain. Distressed by the military use of aircraft, he asked the League of Nations to ban airplanes from warfare.

name: Tiradentes
description: Ensign and dentist who led the Minas Conspiracy against colonial taxation and Portuguese rule. Inspired by American independence, the plot envisioned a republic with a university and local manufacturing; he was hanged in 1792.

name: John D. Rockefeller
description: Founder of Standard Oil, he built the largest industrial monopoly in American history until its breakup by the Supreme Court in 1911. A devout, teetotal Baptist, he became the greatest philanthropist of his era, founding the University of Chicago and the Rockefeller Foundation.

name: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: Russian novelist sentenced to hard labor in Siberia for socialist activity, he converted to a Slavophile, monarchist Orthodox Christianity. In Demons and The Brothers Karamazov he attacked nihilism, atheism and Western rationalism.

name: Thomas Edison
description: American inventor and businessman with over a thousand patents, he created the phonograph, the commercial light bulb and the first industrial research lab. He backed direct current against Tesla and was a deist freethinker critical of organized religion.

name: Franz Kafka
description: German-language Jewish writer from Prague, he portrayed in The Trial and The Castle the individual crushed by opaque bureaucracies and arbitrary authority. A workers' insurance official, he sympathized with Czech anarchists and cultural Zionism.

name: Galileo Galilei
description: Tuscan physicist and astronomer, father of the experimental scientific method, he improved the telescope and defended Copernican heliocentrism. A Catholic, he was condemned by the Inquisition in 1633 and spent his last years under house arrest, under Medici patronage.

name: Thomas Müntzer
description: Radical Reformation preacher who broke with Luther and led peasants and miners in the German Peasants' War of 1525. He preached an apocalyptic theocracy of the elect, with goods in common and the overthrow of godless princes; he was beheaded after Frankenhausen.

name: Paulo Freire
description: Brazilian educator and author of Pedagogy of the Oppressed, he created an adult literacy method based on political consciousness-raising. Exiled by the 1964 dictatorship, he was tied to Liberation Theology and later led São Paulo's schools for the Workers' Party.

name: Romeu Zema
description: Businessman and governor of Minas Gerais for the Novo party (2019–2026), he is a 2026 presidential candidate. He proposes privatizing every state company, leaving BRICS, curbing the Supreme Court, lowering the age of criminal responsibility and banning all abortion.

name: Ronaldo Caiado
description: Orthopedic surgeon, founder of the agribusiness UDR and governor of Goiás (2019–2026), he is the PSD's 2026 presidential candidate. He pledges a hard line on criminal gangs, a broad amnesty for January 8 defendants, spending control and protection of rural property.

name: José Antonio Kast
description: Founder of Chile's Republican Party and president since March 2026, a conservative Catholic who has openly praised Pinochet's legacy. He pledges to expel irregular migrants, toughen sentences, cut spending and lower corporate taxes, and opposes abortion.

name: Yamandú Orsi
description: History teacher, Mujica's political heir in the MPP and president of Uruguay for the Broad Front since 2025. A moderate, consensus-seeking leftist, he pairs stronger social programs and policing with fiscal prudence and no new taxes, and signed a euthanasia law.

name: Santiago Peña
description: Former IMF economist and president of Paraguay for the Colorado Party since 2023, backed by Horacio Cartes. He keeps taxes low, ties with Taiwan and alignment with Trump and Israel, and champions agribusiness and the traditional family.

name: Gavin Newsom
description: Democratic governor of California since 2019 and a 2028 presidential hopeful, he leads state resistance to Trump on immigration, climate and redistricting. A same-sex marriage pioneer in San Francisco, he regulates AI but has cracked down on homeless camps.

name: Jonas Gahr Støre
description: Labour leader and prime minister of Norway since 2021, re-elected in 2025. A pro-NATO social democrat, he keeps the wealth tax and state-owned Equinor, defends oil exploration and recognized Palestine, alongside a restrictive asylum policy.

name: Felipe VI
description: King of Spain since 2014, a militarily trained constitutional monarch. In his 3 October 2017 speech he condemned the Catalan separatist referendum to defend constitutional unity; he renounced his father's inheritance and promotes transparency and Europeanism.

name: Friedrich Merz
description: Christian Democratic chancellor of Germany since 2025 and former head of BlackRock Germany. He tightened migration and border policy, loosened the debt brake to rearm the country and keeps the firewall against the AfD; a Catholic, he is socially conservative.

name: Naruhito
description: Emperor of Japan since 2019, a symbol of the state with no political powers under the pacifist Constitution. An Oxford-trained historian and water-resources expert, he expresses "deep remorse" over the war and champions peace, the environment and international cooperation.

name: Jerome Powell
description: Republican lawyer and former finance executive, Powell chaired the Federal Reserve from 2018 to 2026, fought the pandemic shock and inflation with high rates and defended central bank independence against Trump's pressure.

name: Augusto Cury
description: Psychiatrist and best-selling self-help author, Cury is a 2026 presidential candidate in Brazil for Avante, running on anti-polarization, semi-presidentialism, fiscal balance, entrepreneurship and mental health.

name: Jefferson Davis
description: U.S. senator and secretary of war, Davis presided over the Confederate States during the Civil War, defending secession, states' rights and slavery as the basis of the South's social and economic order.

name: John C. Calhoun
description: U.S. vice president and South Carolina senator, Calhoun formulated the doctrines of nullification and the concurrent majority and defended slavery as a positive good, inspiring Southern secession.

name: Néstor Kirchner
description: Argentine president from 2003 to 2007, Kirchner led the recovery after the 2001 crisis with center-left Peronism: he renegotiated the debt, broke with the IMF, expanded social spending and reopened dictatorship trials.

name: Carlos Menem
description: Argentine president from 1989 to 1999 elected by Peronism, Menem embraced neoliberalism: he privatized state firms, pegged the peso to the dollar, opened the economy, aligned with the US and pardoned junta officers.

name: Sergio Mattarella
description: President of Italy since 2015, re-elected in 2022, Mattarella comes from left-wing Christian Democracy and guards the Constitution, Europeanism, NATO and support for Ukraine, against the Mafia that killed his brother.

name: Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa
description: Law professor, TV commentator and former PSD leader, Marcelo was president of Portugal from 2016 to 2026, with a warm, close-to-the-people style, moderate Catholic conservatism, Europeanism and cooperation with left-wing governments.

name: Baldwin IV
description: Crusader king of Jerusalem from 1174 to 1185, Baldwin IV ruled as a leper from childhood, defeated Saladin at Montgisard, defended the Latin kingdom by faith and sword and kept pragmatic truces with the Muslims.

name: Otto Strasser
description: Brother of Gregor Strasser, he broke with Hitler in 1930 and founded the Black Front, championing an anti-capitalist, federalist and Christian national socialism with land for peasants; exiled, he returned to Germany in 1955.

name: Ahmed al-Sharaa
description: Syria’s interim president since 2025 and former HTS leader, Ahmed al-Sharaa concentrates power during the transition, retains Islam as the main source of law and seeks to reintegrate Kurdish areas and attract investment amid sectarian violence and civil rights concerns.

name: Hafez al-Assad
description: Syrian president from 1971 to 2000, Hafez al-Assad consolidated a militarized authoritarian Ba’athist state, combining Arab socialism, nationalism, single-party rule, patronage and pragmatic regional diplomacy.

name: Reza Pahlavi
description: Son of Iran's last shah and an exiled opposition figure, Reza Pahlavi advocates a secular democratic transition, free elections and a choice between monarchy and republic. He prioritizes territorial integrity, individual liberties and market reforms; he has never governed Iran.

name: Mohammad Reza Pahlavi
description: Iran's last shah (1941–1979), Mohammad Reza Pahlavi consolidated an authoritarian monarchy allied with the West. The White Revolution advanced land reform, industrialization and women's rights, while SAVAK repressed the opposition.

name: Gamal Abdel Nasser
description: Egypt's president from 1956 to 1970, Nasser nationalized the Suez Canal and expanded state ownership and land reform. He championed pan-Arabism and non-alignment while concentrating power and repressing the opposition.

name: Ernst Jünger
description: A World War I veteran and Conservative Revolutionary writer, Jünger praised technological mobilization and criticized bourgeois liberalism in The Worker (1932). He refused to join the Nazi Party and later criticized totalitarianism.

name: Oswald Spengler
description: A Conservative Revolutionary philosopher, Spengler saw civilizations as cyclical in The Decline of the West. He advocated authoritarian, anti-Marxist Prussian socialism; he later criticized Nazism without abandoning nationalism.

name: Ferdinand III of Castile
description: King of Castile from 1217 and León from 1230, he consolidated the union of the crowns and conquered Córdoba and Seville. He ruled as a medieval Catholic monarch and promoted legal and administrative organization in conquered territories.

name: Muhammad Abduh
description: Grand Mufti of Egypt and father of Islamic modernism, Abduh argued for reinterpreting Islam through reason (ijtihad), reformed teaching at Al-Azhar and the religious courts, and opposed both clerical stagnation and British rule.

name: Sayyid Qutb
description: Muslim Brotherhood ideologue, Qutb wrote Milestones, which declared modern Muslim societies to be in jahiliyya and called for a vanguard to establish God's sovereignty. He was executed by Nasser's government in 1966.

name: Averroes
description: Philosopher, physician and judge from Córdoba, Averroes commented on Aristotle and held that philosophical reason and Quranic revelation do not contradict each other, influencing Christian scholasticism. He served the Almohad court and was exiled under pressure from theologians.

name: Alwaleed bin Talal
description: Saudi prince and founder of Kingdom Holding, Alwaleed invested in Citigroup, Twitter, Four Seasons and News Corp and advocated economic opening and women's employment in the kingdom. He was detained in 2017 in Mohammed bin Salman's anti-corruption campaign.

name: Muhammad Ali Jinnah
description: Lawyer and leader of the Muslim League, Jinnah led the creation of Pakistan in 1947 on the two-nation theory and was its first governor-general, advocating a Muslim-majority state with religious freedom for minorities.

name: Saladin
description: Founder of the Ayyubid dynasty, Saladin united Egypt and Syria, defeated the Crusaders at Hattin and retook Jerusalem in 1187, becoming a symbol of jihad against the Crusades and of chivalry recognized even by his enemies.

name: David Ben-Gurion
description: Leader of Labor Zionism and the Mapai party, Ben-Gurion proclaimed Israel's independence in 1948 and was its first prime minister, building a secular, centralized state with a strong public sector, kibbutzim, and the army as the school of the nation.

name: Sergei Melikov
description: A Russian National Guard general and Putin ally, Melikov headed Dagestan from 2020 to 2026, a period marked by war mobilization, the antisemitic airport pogrom, and jihadist attacks, and in 2026 became a senator for Bryansk.

name: Emperor Jimmu
description: The first legendary emperor of Japan according to the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki, Jimmu, a descendant of the sun goddess Amaterasu, is said to have conquered Yamato by force of arms and founded the imperial line, a central myth of State Shinto and Japanese nationalism.

name: Emperor Meiji
description: Emperor under whose 1868 restoration Japan abolished the shogunate and the samurai, centralized the state, industrialized under the slogan "rich country, strong army", adopted the 1889 constitution and State Shinto, and defeated China and Russia.

name: Oda Nobunaga
description: A Sengoku-period daimyo, Nobunaga began the unification of Japan with massed arquebuses, deposed the Ashikaga shogunate, massacred the warrior monks of Enryaku-ji and the Ikko-ikki, abolished guilds and tolls, and tolerated Jesuit missionaries.

name: Qin Shi Huang
description: King of Qin who unified China in 221 BC and proclaimed himself first emperor, he ruled through Legalism with harsh laws, replaced feudalism with centralized commanderies, standardized script and coinage, burned books and began the Great Wall.

name: Charles V
description: Heir of the Habsburgs, Charles V united Spain, the Low Countries, the Holy Roman Empire and the American conquests, fought the Lutheran Reformation and the Ottomans as champion of universal Catholicism, crushed the Comuneros and abdicated in 1556.

name: Salvador Dalí
description: Catalan surrealist painter, Dalí was expelled from the surrealist group over his ambiguous sympathies for fascism, publicly backed Franco and the monarchy and, from 1949 on, embraced a Catholic nuclear mysticism fusing faith and science.

name: Pablo Picasso
description: Spanish painter and co-founder of Cubism, Picasso painted Guernica against the Francoist bombing, joined the French Communist Party in 1944, backed the Soviet-led peace movement and never returned to Franco's Spain.

name: Albert Camus
description: French-Algerian writer and 1957 Nobel laureate, Camus fought in the Resistance, broke with Sartre by condemning the Soviet camps in The Rebel and defended a plural Algeria against terrorism on both sides.

name: Victor Gao
description: Former Deng Xiaoping interpreter and vice president of the CCG think tank, Victor Gao defends one-party rule, unifying Taiwan by any means, Hong Kong's security law and the claim that NATO caused the war in Ukraine.

name: 13th Dalai Lama (Thubten Gyatso)
description: Head of theocratic Tibet, the 13th Dalai Lama expelled the Chinese and proclaimed independence in 1913, built an army, post and currency, backed down before the monasteries by closing the English school, and warned against communism in 1932.

name: Abraham Isaac Kook
description: First Ashkenazi chief rabbi of Mandatory Palestine, Kook was the leading theologian of religious Zionism, saw secular pioneers as instruments of the divine plan and holiness in the Land of Israel, and founded the Mercaz HaRav yeshiva.

name: Louis Auguste Blanqui
description: French revolutionary and conspirator, Blanqui argued that an organized minority should seize power by insurrection and impose a provisional dictatorship, spent over thirty years in prison, was elected to the Paris Commune from his cell and took the motto "Neither God nor master".

name: S. W. R. D. Bandaranaike
description: Prime Minister of Ceylon from 1956 to 1959, he converted to Buddhism, founded the Freedom Party, nationalized ports and buses, made Sinhala the official language, pursued non-alignment and was assassinated by a Buddhist monk.

name: Joseph II of Austria
description: Holy Roman Emperor and Archduke of Austria, Joseph II abolished personal serfdom, decreed religious tolerance, closed hundreds of monasteries, imposed German on the administration and saw his reforms provoke revolts, in Belgium and Hungary.

name: King David
description: According to the Bible, David united the tribes of Israel, conquered Jerusalem and made it his capital, defeated the Philistines, brought the Ark to the city and built a centralized kingdom, and tradition attributes the Psalms to him and the line of the Messiah.

name: Olaf Scholz
description: A Social Democrat and German chancellor from 2021 to 2025, Scholz proclaimed the Zeitenwende, with 100 billion euros for the armed forces and weapons for Ukraine, raised the minimum wage to 12 euros and defended the debt brake until the traffic-light coalition collapsed.

name: Jimmy Carter
description: A Democratic president and devout Baptist (1977–81), Carter made human rights the core of foreign policy, deregulated airlines and transport, brokered Camp David, returned the Panama Canal and fell after the Iran hostage crisis and stagflation.

name: Lyndon B. Johnson
description: A Democratic president from 1963 to 1969, Johnson launched the Great Society and the war on poverty, created Medicare and Medicaid and signed the Civil Rights and Voting Rights Acts, but escalated the Vietnam War, which destroyed his popularity.

name: Helmut Kohl
description: A Christian Democrat of the CDU and chancellor for 16 years (1982–98), Kohl led German reunification, deepened European integration through the Maastricht Treaty and the euro, made moderate liberalizing reforms and fell after the secret donations scandal.

name: Mark Carney
description: A former governor of the Bank of Canada and the Bank of England, Carney has been Liberal prime minister since 2025: he scrapped the consumer carbon tax, fast-tracked pipelines and major projects, raised defence spending and retaliated against Trump's tariffs.

name: Boris Johnson
description: A Conservative and Brexit leader, prime minister from 2019 to 2022, Johnson took the UK out of the EU, armed Ukraine, raised taxes and public spending, opened non-EU immigration and fell after Partygate; he is now a Daily Mail columnist.

name: James Cook
description: A Royal Navy officer and cartographer, Cook led three scientific expeditions to the Pacific, charted New Zealand and the east coast of Australia, claimed lands in the name of the Crown, fought scurvy and died in a clash with Hawaiians.

name: Lachlan Macquarie
description: Colonial governor of New South Wales (1810–21), Macquarie replaced military rule with public works and town planning, granted land and office to freed convicts and founded schools for Aboriginal people, but ordered the Appin massacre against resisters.

name: Andy Burnham
description: UK Prime Minister since 2026, Labour's Burnham advocates devolution, electoral reform, public control of essential services and closer EU ties. He supports Ukraine, border control and LGBT rights, influenced by Catholic social teaching.

name: Anthony Albanese
description: Australian Labor prime minister since 2022, he expands Medicare and public housing, maintains AUKUS, tightens temporary visas and banned social media for under-16s, while defending multiculturalism and free trade.

name: Gustavus Adolphus
description: King of Sweden from 1611 to 1632, Gustavus Adolphus reformed the army with linear infantry and light artillery, made Sweden a Baltic power and entered the Thirty Years' War as a Lutheran champion, dying at Lützen.

name: Charles X Gustav
description: King of Sweden from 1654 to 1660, Charles X Gustav invaded Poland and Denmark, crossed the frozen Belts in 1658 and imposed the Treaty of Roskilde, taking the empire to its greatest extent and beginning the reduction of noble lands.

name: Henry VIII
description: King of England from 1509 to 1547, Henry VIII broke with Rome through the Act of Supremacy (1534), became head of the Church of England, dissolved the monasteries, centralized power in the Crown under Thomas Cromwell and executed opponents such as Thomas More.

name: Wilhelm II of Germany
description: Last German emperor and king of Prussia (1888–1918), Wilhelm II dismissed Bismarck, pursued Weltpolitik with the High Seas Fleet, militarism and colonial expansion, led Germany into the First World War and abdicated in 1918, going into exile in the Netherlands.

name: Constantine the Great
description: Roman emperor from 306 to 337, Constantine reunified the Empire, granted freedom to Christians in the Edict of Milan (313), convened the Council of Nicaea (325), founded Constantinople and reorganized the state with a mobile army and fiscal reforms.

name: Vladimir the Great
description: Grand Prince of Kyiv from 980 to 1015, Vladimir the Great unified and expanded Kievan Rus', ended paganism by adopting Byzantine Orthodox Christianity in 988, married the Byzantine princess Anna and had his people baptized in the Dnieper.

name: Desmond Tutu
description: A South African Anglican archbishop and 1984 Nobel Peace Prize laureate, Tutu led nonviolent campaigns against apartheid and chaired the Truth and Reconciliation Commission. He advocated human rights and public reconciliation on the basis of his Christian faith.

name: Russell Kirk
description: An American political philosopher and historian, Kirk influenced postwar conservatism with The Conservative Mind (1953). He championed tradition, historical continuity, political prudence, local communities, and a moral order rooted in religion.

name: Nikita Khrushchev
description: First Secretary of the Soviet Communist Party (1953–1964) and premier of the USSR (1958–1964), Khrushchev denounced Stalin and began de-Stalinization while retaining one-party rule. His government launched Sputnik and confronted the United States during the Cuban Missile Crisis.

name: Sigmund Freud
description: Austrian neurologist who founded psychoanalysis and developed concepts such as the unconscious, repression, and the Oedipus complex. In The Future of an Illusion and Civilization and Its Discontents, he critically examined religion, culture, and conflicts between individual desire and social life.

name: Jean-Paul Marat
description: A physician and journalist of the French Revolution, Marat edited L’Ami du peuple and advocated popular sovereignty, exceptional measures against counterrevolution, and vigilance over rulers. In The Chains of Slavery (1774), he denounced monarchical despotism.

name: Grigory Zinoviev
description: A Bolshevik leader, Zinoviev chaired the Communist International from 1919 to 1926 and led the party in Leningrad. An ally of Stalin against Trotsky after Lenin’s death, he was later convicted in a show trial and executed during the Great Purge.

name: Dante Alighieri
description: A Florentine poet involved in municipal politics, Dante argued in De Monarchia for a universal imperial authority independent of the papacy’s temporal power. Exile after Florence’s factional disputes shaped his view of political order.

name: John IV of Portugal
description: The Duke of Braganza acclaimed king after the Restoration of 1640, John IV ended the Iberian Union and led Portugal in war against Spain to recover its independence. He founded the Braganza dynasty and sought diplomatic alliances to sustain the new kingdom.

name: Charles I of England
description: The Stuart king defended royal prerogative and the divine right of monarchs. His conflicts with Parliament over taxes and authority, alongside his attempt to impose Anglican practices in Scotland, contributed to the Wars of the Three Kingdoms and his execution in 1649.

name: Pythagoras
description: A Greek philosopher and community leader in southern Italy, Pythagoras linked mathematics and cosmology to religious discipline. Later accounts connect Pythagoreans to political influence in Magna Graecia, though his own ideas are hard to separate from those of his followers.

name: Epicurus
description: A Greek philosopher who taught that happiness depends on the absence of pain and disturbance, supported by friendship and moderate desires. He understood justice as a useful agreement to neither harm nor be harmed, and advised avoiding political strife where possible.

name: Heraclitus
description: A philosopher from Ephesus known for fragments on change, opposition, and the logos that orders the world. His texts relate human law to a common order, but the scarcity of sources makes any reconstruction of his specific political positions controversial.

name: Democritus
description: Greek philosopher from Abdera who, with Leucippus, developed an atomist account of nature in which reality consists of atoms and void. His writings also addressed ethics and politics.

name: Diogenes of Sinope
description: Greek philosopher from Sinope and the leading figure of ancient Cynicism, he championed self-sufficiency and a simple life in accordance with nature, challenging social convention, wealth, and authority through provocation.

name: Seneca
description: Roman Stoic philosopher and statesman, Seneca advised Nero and wrote about clemency, virtue, and mastery of the passions; his proximity to power and great wealth stand in tension with his counsel of simplicity.

name: Epictetus
description: Greek Stoic philosopher, born enslaved in the Roman Empire, he taught that freedom depends on distinguishing what is within our control and cultivating virtue. His student Arrian recorded his lessons.

name: Oliver Cromwell
description: Parliamentarian commander and Lord Protector of England, Cromwell took part in the execution of Charles I and consolidated a centralized Puritan republic; his campaigns in Ireland and Scotland extended English power.

name: Ignatius of Loyola
description: A Basque nobleman who became a priest, Ignatius of Loyola founded the Society of Jesus and wrote the Spiritual Exercises, a method of prayer that shaped Jesuit formation and missionary activity.

name: Linus Torvalds
description: Finnish-American software engineer, he started the Linux kernel in 1991 and created Git in 2005; his technical leadership and open development made these projects central to digital infrastructure.

name: Francis I of Austria
description: The last Holy Roman Emperor and first Emperor of Austria, Francis I founded the Austrian Empire in 1804. Allied with Metternich, he suppressed liberal movements and supported the post-Napoleonic conservative order.

name: Luiz Felipe Pondé
description: Brazilian philosopher and columnist, Pondé describes himself as a liberal conservative: he supports economic and civil liberties, criticizes moral progressivism and both left- and right-wing populism, and studies religion without adhering to a tradition.

name: Mark Fisher
description: British cultural theorist, Fisher developed the concept of capitalist realism to examine the difficulty of imagining alternatives to capitalism. He connected culture, mental health and neoliberalism, and outlined acid communism.

name: Alex Williams
description: British political theorist, Williams co-wrote the accelerationist manifesto and Inventing the Future with Nick Srnicek. He advocates automation, shorter working hours and a basic income as part of a postcapitalist left strategy.

name: Enrico Berlinguer
description: As leader of the Italian Communist Party, Berlinguer advocated a democratic, pluralist path to socialism, distanced himself from the Soviet model, and proposed the Historic Compromise with Christian Democrats.

name: Pier Paolo Pasolini
description: Italian Marxist writer and filmmaker, Pasolini defended Friulian cultural autonomy and criticized consumerism and social homogenization. Persecuted for his homosexuality, he also opposed the liberalization of abortion.

name: Per Albin Hansson
description: Swedish prime minister, Hansson promoted the folkhemmet through parliamentary welfare and employment reforms. He combined a mixed economy, compromise with farmers and employers, and armed neutrality during the Second World War.

name: Kalevi Sorsa
description: Finnish social democratic prime minister, Sorsa expanded public services and social protection, promoted agreements among government, unions and employers, and combined European trade integration with Cold War neutrality.

name: Tage Erlander
description: Swedish prime minister from 1946 to 1969, Erlander expanded public pensions, healthcare and education within a mixed economy. He combined collective bargaining, industrial modernization and international neutrality with strong military defence.

name: Einar Gerhardsen
description: Norwegian Labour prime minister, Gerhardsen rebuilt the country through economic planning, public services and collective bargaining. He consolidated parliamentary democracy and joined NATO while rejecting nuclear weapons on Norwegian soil.

name: Gösta Rehn
description: Swedish economist, Rehn co-developed the Rehn–Meidner model, combining full employment, wage solidarity and price stability. He advocated worker retraining, social protection and productive modernization within a mixed economy.

name: Eduard Limonov
description: Russian writer and National Bolshevik Party founder, Limonov combined socialism, imperial expansionism and cultural rebellion. He opposed Putin’s repression but supported Crimea’s annexation and separatist forces in Donbas.

name: Nicola Bombacci
description: A cofounder of the Communist Party of Italy, he later moved toward Mussolini. In the Italian Social Republic, he promoted the socialization of enterprises and workers’ participation while retaining his anticapitalist rhetoric.

name: Corneliu Zelea Codreanu
description: Founder of Romania’s Iron Guard, Codreanu combined fascism, violent antisemitism and Orthodox Christian mysticism. He advocated authoritarian leadership, national regeneration and communal organization of peasants and workers.

name: Oswald Mosley
description: Founder of the British Union of Fascists, he advocated authoritarian government, corporatism and protectionism. He promoted antisemitism and, after the war, pan-European nationalism and racial segregation.

name: Michel Aflaq
description: A Baath cofounder, Aflaq advocated Arab unity, anticolonial socialism and spiritual renewal inspired by Islam. He rejected Marxist materialism and criticized military dictatorship, while associating with the Iraqi Baath.

name: Ramiro Ledesma Ramos
description: A philosopher and founder of the JONS, Ledesma formulated Spanish national syndicalism, combining national revolution, worker mobilization and an authoritarian state. He opposed communism and separatism and criticized monarchy and parliamentarism.

name: Gabriele D'Annunzio
description: An Italian poet and nationalist, he led the 1919 occupation of Fiume and governed the Regency of Carnaro. The Charter of Carnaro, drafted with Alceste De Ambris, combined corporatism, social rights and popular sovereignty.

name: Alain de Benoist
description: A French intellectual and founder of the Nouvelle Droite and GRECE, he advocates cultural autonomy and ethnopluralism, opposes mass immigration, and criticizes liberalism, capitalism and global homogenization. He proposes European paganism as a cultural alternative to Christianity.

name: Léon Degrelle
description: Leader of Belgium's Catholic Rexist movement, he became a Nazi collaborator during the occupation and commanded Walloon volunteers in the Waffen-SS. After the war, he lived in exile in Spain and remained an admirer of Hitler.

name: Gustavo Barroso
description: A Brazilian writer and Integralism leader, Barroso headed the Brazilian Integralist Action militia and promoted authoritarian nationalism and conspiratorial antisemitism, in contrast with Plínio Salgado's more moderate line.

name: Hugh MacDiarmid
description: A central poet of the Scottish Renaissance and advocate of Scottish independence, MacDiarmid combined cultural nationalism with revolutionary socialism and communist internationalism.

name: John Maclean
description: A Scottish teacher and revolutionary Marxist, Maclean organized workers and opposed the First World War. He advocated an independent Scottish socialist republic and taught Marxist economics to workers.

name: James Connolly
description: A Marxist socialist and trade unionist, Connolly founded the Irish Socialist Republican Party and linked national independence to social transformation. He led during the 1916 Easter Rising and was executed after its defeat.

name: Lorenzo de’ Medici
description: De facto ruler of Florence from 1469, Lorenzo balanced diplomacy among the Italian powers and consolidated Medici influence. A poet and humanist, he gathered artists and philosophers at his court.

name: Filippo Brunelleschi
description: The Florentine architect and engineer designed the dome of Santa Maria del Fiore Cathedral and projects such as the Ospedale degli Innocenti. He studied ancient buildings and applied mathematical principles to architecture.

name: Leonardo da Vinci
description: The Florentine artist and investigator worked for courts such as the Sforza in Milan and served Cesare Borgia as a military engineer. His notebooks record studies of anatomy, mechanics, hydraulics, and drawing.

name: Sandro Botticelli
description: Associated with the Medici court in Florence, Botticelli painted works such as The Birth of Venus and Primavera. He also produced religious paintings and worked late in life amid Savonarola’s preaching.

name: Michelangelo Buonarroti
description: The Florentine sculptor, painter, and architect created David, the Pietà, and the Sistine Chapel frescoes. He worked for popes and the Medici and took part in Florence’s defense during the republic of 1529.

name: Raphael
description: The painter and architect from Urbino worked in Florence and Rome for Popes Julius II and Leo X. His Vatican frescoes and studies of antiquity helped shape High Renaissance art.

name: Thomas Carlyle
description: Scottish essayist and historian who criticized classical liberalism as the dismal science and formulated the Great Man theory, championing heroic leadership and hierarchical order over modern egalitarianism.

name: Hans-Adam II
description: Sovereign Prince of Liechtenstein since 1989 and author of The State in the Third Millennium, advocating local self-determination down to the municipal level, constitutional monarchy, and free markets.

name: Dom Bertrand
description: Spokesman for the Vassouras branch of the Brazilian imperial family and TFP-aligned activist, advocating the restoration of a Catholic parliamentary monarchy, rural property rights, and traditional values.

name: Aleksandr Lukashenko
description: President of Belarus since 1994, ruling through an authoritarian, personalist regime that combines strong state economic control, military alliance with Russia, and systematic repression of opposition.

name: Giovanni Giolitti
description: Five-time Prime Minister of liberal Italy who governed through pragmatic transformism, expanded universal male suffrage, and introduced social reforms integrating moderate socialists.

name: Aldo Moro
description: Christian Democracy leader and Italian Prime Minister who orchestrated the opening to the left and the Historic Compromise with the Communist Party, later kidnapped and killed by the Red Brigades.

name: Silvio Berlusconi
description: Media tycoon and four-time Prime Minister of Italy who founded Forza Italia, ushering in an era of center-right media populism that combined economic liberalism and conservative social politics.

name: Juan Bautista Alberdi
description: A jurist of the Generation of '37, Alberdi wrote the Bases (1852), the blueprint of Argentina's 1853 Constitution, advocating federalism with a strong executive, free trade, foreign capital and European immigration under the motto "to govern is to populate".

name: Julio Argentino Roca
description: General and twice president of Argentina, Roca led the Desert Campaign against Indigenous peoples, federalized Buenos Aires and headed the Generation of '80: a centralized state, secular schooling, European immigration and an agro-export economy.

name: Rupert Murdoch
description: Media magnate and founder of News Corp and Fox News, he backed Thatcher and the Iraq invasion. He advocates free markets, global trade and immigration alongside conservative cultural values.

name: Gabriel Boric
description: Former student leader and president of Chile from 2022 to 2026, he represents the new Latin American left: an ecological focus, expanded social rights, unqualified defense of human rights and criticism of authoritarian regimes.

name: Gustavo Petro
description: Economist and Colombia's first left-wing president (2022-2026). He prioritized the ecological transition away from fossil fuels, the Total Peace policy with guerrillas and distributive reforms in healthcare and pensions.

name: Donald Tusk
description: Leader of Civic Platform and former European Council President, returning to office in 2023: champion of EU integration, democratic rule of law and robust NATO collective defense against Russian aggression.

name: Andrzej Duda
description: President of Poland from 2015 to 2025, aligned with the Law and Justice party (PiS). He champions traditional Catholic family values, a sovereign strengthening of the Polish armed forces and a firm alliance with the United States and NATO.

name: Shigeru Ishiba
description: Japanese Prime Minister and LDP leader, defense specialist. He advocates for a more self-reliant security posture, an Asian NATO concept, rural revitalization and prudent fiscal policies.

name: Cyril Ramaphosa
description: Former trade union leader, businessman and South African President since 2018 for the ANC. He balances industrial growth, constitutional land reform, pragmatism in foreign trade and multilateral BRICS diplomacy.

name: Miguel Díaz-Canel
description: First Secretary of the Communist Party and President of Cuba, succeeding Raúl Castro in 2018: maintains one-party socialist state planning while allowing measured private micro-enterprise reforms.

name: Tô Lâm
description: General Secretary of Vietnam's Communist Party and former Public Security Minister. He oversees a socialist-oriented market economy, tech modernization, anti-corruption campaigns and balanced non-aligned diplomacy.

name: Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan
description: Ruler of Abu Dhabi and UAE President since 2022. Architect of the Emirates' economic and military rise, he drove the Abraham Accords with Israel, post-oil technological diversification and controlled modernization.

name: Keir Starmer
description: Labour leader and UK Prime Minister from 2024 to 2026, he resigned after an internal party revolt. Former chief prosecutor, he emphasizes fiscal discipline, public clean energy, rebuilt public services and pragmatic ties with the EU.

name: David Friedman
description: Economist and physicist who pioneered consequentialist anarcho-capitalism: argues that law, courts and police can be efficiently provided by competitive free markets without relying on natural rights.

name: Henry Hazlitt
description: American economic journalist and philosopher associated with the Austrian School, celebrated for popularizing free-market economics and exposing the unseen costs of government price controls and subsidies.

name: David Graeber
description: Anthropologist and anarchist activist, leading figure of Occupy Wall Street: explored the moral origins of debt and money, attacked corporate bureaucracy and advocated for direct consensus democracy.

name: Ricardo Flores Magón
description: Mexican journalist and revolutionary who led the magonismo movement and the PLM: fought for the abolition of state power and private property under the slogan Tierra y Libertad against the Díaz dictatorship.

name: Gustav Landauer
description: German anarchist philosopher of the Bavarian Soviet Republic: argued that the state is a social relationship overcome by building voluntary cooperative communities, rejecting orthodox Marxist dogma.

name: Guy Debord
description: French author and filmmaker, founder of the Situationist International: formulated the critique of the society of the spectacle, where authentic human life is replaced by commodified media images.

name: Alexander Berkman
description: Russian-American writer and militant, companion of Emma Goldman: championed direct revolutionary action and stateless libertarian communism while exposing Bolshevik repression during the Russian Revolution.

name: Carlos Marighella
description: Constituent congressman and founder of the National Liberation Action (ALN), he broke with the orthodox PCB to wage urban armed struggle against the Brazilian military dictatorship.

name: Josiah Warren
description: Widely regarded as the first American individualist anarchist, he founded the Cincinnati Time Store, pioneering commerce based on labor notes exchanging goods for the cost of production, advocating individual sovereignty and total separation from the State.

name: John Mackey
description: Co-founder and former CEO of Whole Foods Market, he articulated and popularized Conscious Capitalism, arguing that free markets and for-profit businesses best create voluntary value for customers, workers, suppliers, and investors without state coercion.

name: Alfried Krupp
description: German industrialist and head of the Krupp steel and arms dynasty, representing the deep integration of heavy manufacturing with the National Socialist war economy, symbolizing militarized state corporatism.

name: Henry Clay Frick
description: American coke and steel magnate and chairman of Carnegie Steel, renowned for uncompromising resistance to organized labor and deploying armed force during the 1892 Homestead Strike, securing unchecked managerial dominance.

name: Andrew Carnegie
description: Leader of the massive expansion of the American steel industry and one of the wealthiest individuals in history, he championed relentless competitive capitalism in The Gospel of Wealth alongside the moral obligation to redistribute wealth through public libraries and education.

name: Kazuo Inamori
description: Founder of Kyocera and KDDI and turnaround leader of Japan Airlines, who established the Kyocera Philosophy and the Amoeba Management System, aligning corporate performance with ethical social responsibility and Buddhist altruism.

name: Adriano Olivetti
description: Italian industrialist leading Olivetti who made his Ivrea factories a global model of industrial humanism, creating the Community Movement to decentralize power into self-governing local communities integrating workers into management, culture, and architecture.

name: Robert Owen
description: Welsh textile industrialist at New Lanark and founder of New Harmony, who demonstrated that decent working conditions, universal child education, and cooperative labor were fully compatible with industrial output, inspiring the modern cooperative and labor movements.

name: Aldo Rebelo
description: Brazilian politician and writer who served as president of the Chamber of Deputies and federal minister. Known for nationalist sovereignty, defense of Amazonian development and agribusiness, and staunch opposition to foreign environmental NGOs.

name: Luiz Philippe de Orleans e Bragança
description: Brazilian federal congressman, political scientist, and monarchist activist descending from the imperial family. He advocates free-market economic reforms, federalist decentralization, state deregulation, and conservative institutional principles.

name: Eduardo Paes
description: Brazilian politician and former multi-term mayor of Rio de Janeiro. Characterized by pragmatic centrist governance, fiscal administration centered on large-scale urban infrastructure investments, public-private partnerships, and broad institutional coalition-building.

name: Joe Rogan
description: American comedian and podcaster, host of The Joe Rogan Experience. Anti-establishment populist-libertarian style, unrestricted free speech and institutional skepticism; in 2026 he broke with Trump over the Iran war and ICE policy.

name: Tucker Carlson
description: American conservative political commentator and journalist. Prominent voice of right-wing nationalist populism, known for staunch opposition to immigration and foreign military intervention, alongside sharp critiques of corporate elites.

name: Ben Shapiro
description: American conservative political commentator, attorney, and co-founder of The Daily Wire. Known for staunch defense of free-market capitalism, Judeo-Christian traditional moral values, assertive Zionism, and sharp debate against the political left.

name: Hasan Piker
description: Turkish-American democratic socialist streamer and commentator (HasanAbi). Champions labor unions and anti-imperialism, sharply criticizes Israel, praises China's model and backs the Democratic left, such as AOC.

name: Glenn Greenwald
description: American investigative journalist and author based in Brazil, co-founder of The Intercept. Known for defending civil liberties, privacy against mass state surveillance, and exposing abuses of power across the political and judicial spectrum.

name: Eduardo Moreira
description: Brazilian economist, author, and communicator, founder of the ICL media network. Former investment banker known for criticizing financial speculation and neoliberalism, advocating redistributive social reforms and national sovereignty.

name: Jones Manoel
description: Brazilian Marxist historian, communicator, and author. Known for popularizing Marxism-Leninism, revitalizing anticolonial revolutionary thought, critiquing liberal reformism, and advocating socialist revolution and working-class power.

name: Guilherme Freire
description: Catholic philosopher and educator, a PUC-SP master's graduate and creator of Filosofia do Zero. He teaches Aristotle and Aquinas, criticizes relativism and the centralization of the state, and sees the 1889 Republic as the origin of Brazil's political crisis.

name: Nando Moura
description: Brazilian musician, political commentator, and digital influencer. Known for an outspoken, impassioned style defending Christian moral conservatism, combating political corruption, and harshly critiquing both the political left and Bolsonarism.

name: Raphaël Lima
description: Brazilian political communicator and activist, founder of the Ideias Radicais channel. Known for popularizing anarcho-capitalism and Austrian economics, advocating strict private property rights, free-market deregulation, and political secession.

name: João Campos
description: Brazilian engineer and politician from the PSB, former mayor of Recife, re-elected with record margins. Known for modern digital communication and public management focused on urban revitalization, slope stabilization, and public nursery expansion.

name: Álvaro Uribe
description: President of Colombia from 2002 to 2010. Known for his Democratic Security doctrine combating FARC insurgencies and drug cartels, paired with free-market reforms, foreign investment promotion, and close strategic alignment with the United States.

name: Shinzo Abe
description: Longest-serving Prime Minister of Japan. Prominent voice of conservative nationalism, known for the Abenomics economic program (monetary easing, fiscal stimulus, structural reform), and advocating constitutional security normalization across the Indo-Pacific.

name: José Carlos Mariátegui
description: Peruvian journalist and Marxist thinker who founded the journal Amauta and the Peruvian Socialist Party. In Seven Interpretive Essays he argued for an Andean socialism rooted in the indigenous community and attacked the latifundio and Lima centralism.

name: Kwame Nkrumah
description: Leader of Ghana's independence in 1957, Nkrumah preached Pan-Africanism and African socialism, nationalized part of the economy and set up a one-party state. He denounced neocolonialism and was overthrown by a coup in 1966.

name: Amílcar Cabral
description: Leader of the PAIGC, Cabral led the armed struggle for independence of Guinea-Bissau and Cape Verde against Portugal, joining Marxism, African nationalism and the analysis of culture. He urged the petty bourgeoisie's 'class suicide'. He was assassinated in 1973.

name: Ali al-Sistani
description: Iraq's top Shia authority, Grand Ayatollah Sistani upholds the quietist tradition, rejects Tehran's rule of the jurist, demanded direct elections in 2004, calls for weapons only in the state's hands and rarely but decisively intervenes in politics.

name: Norodom Sihanouk
description: King and later head of state of Cambodia, Sihanouk won independence from France in 1953, practiced a neutral Buddhist socialism in the Cold War, was deposed in 1970, allied with the Khmer Rouge and returned as king in 1993.

name: Boris III da Bulgária
description: Tsar of Bulgaria from 1918 to 1943, Boris III took authoritarian personal rule after the 1934 coup, allied with the Axis without sending troops against the USSR and resisted deporting Bulgarian Jews. He died in 1943 in disputed circumstances.

name: Jan III Sobieski
description: King of Poland-Lithuania from 1674 to 1696, Sobieski was the commander who led the victory over the Ottomans at the Battle of Vienna in 1683. A devout Catholic, he reigned over a noble republic without managing to strengthen the state against the magnates.

name: Józef Piłsudski
description: A former socialist and hero of the 1920 war against the Soviets, Piłsudski was head of state of restored Poland. He seized power in a 1926 coup and ruled authoritatively, with a nationalist, anti-communist regime and a regional federation concept.

name: Georges Danton
description: An orator and leader of the French Revolution, Danton helped topple the monarchy, organized the Republic's defense in 1792 and led the first Committee of Public Safety. He called for ending the Terror and was guillotined by Robespierre in 1794.

name: Bob Marley
description: Reggae and Rastafari icon, Marley carried messages of resistance, social justice and Pan-Africanism to the world, united Jamaica's political rivals in 1978 and made his songs an anthem of liberation for the oppressed and rejection of mental colonialism.

name: Abdullah II da Jordânia
description: King of Jordan since 1999, Abdullah II concentrates power over government, army and foreign policy, keeps peace with Israel and the Western alliance and pushes liberal economic reforms, while restricting the opposition and banning the Muslim Brotherhood in 2025.

name: Qaboos bin Said
description: Sultan of Oman from 1970 to 2020, Qaboos deposed his father, modernized the country with oil income, ruled as an absolute monarch and adopted a foreign policy of neutrality and mediation, grounded in the Ibadi tradition of tolerance.

name: Nasser al-Din Shah Qajar
description: Qajar monarch who ruled Persia for nearly half a century, introducing telegraphs, postal services, and photography while navigating British and Russian colonial rivalries.

name: Count of Cavour
description: Piedmontese statesman and architect of Italian unification, championing constitutional liberalism, railway infrastructure, and international diplomacy during the Risorgimento.

name: Leopold I of Tuscany
description: Enlightened Habsburg-Lorraine monarch who abolished capital punishment and torture in Tuscany, deregulated trade, and enacted pioneering legal and agrarian reforms.

name: Ludwig II of Bavaria
description: Bavarian monarch renowned for patronage of Richard Wagner and fairy-tale castles like Neuschwanstein, fiercely defending Bavarian cultural autonomy and Catholic identity.

name: Frederick Augustus I of Saxony
description: First King of Saxony, known as The Just, who led his nation through the Napoleonic Wars and fostered early German industrial and textile modernization.

name: Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies
description: Bourbon monarch who reigned through revolutionary and Napoleonic upheavals, sustained by popular Catholic devotion and royalist counter-revolutionary resistance.

name: Victor Emmanuel III
description: House of Savoy monarch who reigned over Italy during World War I, the rise and fall of Mussolini's fascist regime, and World War II, abdicating in 1946.

name: Christian IV of Denmark
description: Renaissance monarch of the Nordic dual kingdom who expanded naval power, founded cities like modern Oslo, intervened in the Thirty Years' War, and promoted trade.

name: George I of Great Britain
description: House of Hanover ruler who united his German electorate with the British Crown under the Act of Settlement, cementing Protestant succession and parliamentary cabinet governance.

name: Eleftherios Venizelos
description: Prominent Greek liberal statesman who spearheaded territorial doubling through the Balkan Wars, pursued the Megali Idea, and allied Greece with the Entente in World War I.

name: Swami Vivekananda
description: A Hindu monk and disciple of Ramakrishna, Vivekananda brought Vedanta to the West at the 1893 Parliament of Religions, defended the unity of religions, service to the poor as worship and an Indian national revival based on spirituality and education.

name: Sri Aurobindo
description: A revolutionary who championed India's complete independence and later withdrew to yoga, Aurobindo developed 'integral yoga' and a philosophy of humanity's spiritual evolution, wrote The Life Divine and inspired the Auroville community.

name: Adi Shankaracharya
description: An eighth-century philosopher and monk, Shankara systematized Advaita Vedanta, which teaches the identity of the self with the absolute (Brahman) and the illusory nature of the world (maya), founded monasteries across India and reorganized Hinduism in the face of Buddhism.

name: Chanakya
description: Adviser to Chandragupta and attributed author of the Arthashastra, Chanakya (Kautilya) set out a doctrine of a strong monarchical state, with espionage, a regulated economy, a standing army and the mandala theory of states, in which the neighbor is a potential rival.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru
description: The first head of government of independent India, Nehru built a secular democratic republic, adopted Fabian-inspired socialist planning and state industrialization, led the Non-Aligned Movement and faced the conflicts over Kashmir and with China.

name: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
description: India's first deputy prime minister and home minister, Patel, the 'Iron Man', integrated more than 560 princely states into the new country by persuasion and force, built the Indian civil service and defended order, private property and a strong unitary state.

name: V. D. Savarkar
description: A revolutionary imprisoned in the Andaman Islands and later Hindu Mahasabha leader, Savarkar formulated Hindutva, the idea that India is the fatherland and holy land of Hindus, defended militarizing the Hindu nation and rational modernization, though personally an atheist.

name: Atal Bihari Vajpayee
description: A poet and three-time prime minister, Vajpayee headed the BJP's first stable coalition, opened the economy with privatizations and infrastructure, tested nuclear weapons in 1998 and sought peace with Pakistan, balancing Hindu nationalism and moderation.

name: Sukarno
description: The independence leader and first president of Indonesia, Sukarno created Pancasila, combined nationalism, religion and communism in Nasakom, instituted 'Guided Democracy', led the Bandung Conference and nonalignment and was ousted by Suharto after 1965.

name: Amartya Sen
description: A 1998 economics Nobel laureate, Sen formulated the capability approach, which measures development by people's real freedom, defends public investment in health and education, democracy as a safeguard against famine and criticizes Hindu nationalism and growth without equity.

name: Narendra Modi
description: Prime Minister of India since 2014 and BJP leader, Modi joins Hindu nationalism, market reforms and digital infrastructure with protectionism and welfare, centralizes power, revoked Kashmir's autonomy and defends India's strategic autonomy.

name: Ashoka
description: A Maurya emperor who ruled nearly all of India, Ashoka conquered Kalinga in 261 BCE and, shaken by the massacre, embraced Buddhism and the dhamma, a policy of nonviolence, tolerance and welfare proclaimed in stone edicts, without abolishing the army or the death penalty.

name: Akbar
description: Mughal emperor from 1556 to 1605, Akbar expanded the empire across most of northern India, centralized administration through the mansabdari system, abolished the jizya, adopted religious tolerance (sulh-i-kul) and created the syncretic faith Din-i Ilahi.

name: Ibrahim Traoré
description: Transitional President of Burkina Faso and military captain who assumed power in 2022, championing a pan-Africanist discourse inspired by Thomas Sankara, terminating French military pacts, and co-founding the Alliance of Sahel States.

name: Jean-Luc Mélenchon
description: Leader of La France Insoumise (LFI) and 2027 presidential candidate, advocating a 6th Republic via constituent assembly, ecological planning, economic interventionism, strict secularism and a gradual exit from NATO.

name: Jean-Marie Le Pen
description: Founder and historic leader of the National Front (FN), pioneer of modern French right-wing populism centered on 'national preference', strict immigration controls, cultural chauvinism, and anti-globalism.

name: Éric Zemmour
description: Journalist and founder of Reconquête, 2027 presidential candidate. Advocates identity nationalism, remigration, a ban on religious symbols, national law over European treaties and lower business taxes.

name: Philippe Pétain
description: Verdun military hero and head of the collaborationist Vichy regime, instituting the authoritarian corporatist 'National Revolution' under the motto 'Work, Family, Fatherland', abolishing republican institutions.

name: François Mitterrand
description: First socialist president of the French Fifth Republic, who united the left, abolished the death penalty, implemented historic nationalizations, and advanced decentralization alongside the Maastricht Treaty.

name: Jacques Chirac
description: Leading figure of republican Gaullism and two-term French president, blending defense of the French social model and pragmatic privatization with assertive diplomatic independence in refusing the 2003 Iraq War.

name: Thomas Malthus
description: Anglican cleric and British economist, author of An Essay on the Principle of Population (1798): he argued that population outgrows food supply and defended moral restraint and reform of the Poor Laws.

name: Paulo Kogos
description: Brazilian right-libertarian activist and YouTuber, Kogos blends Hoppean anarcho-capitalism and Austrian economics with sedevacantist traditionalist Catholicism, rejecting democracy for natural elites and monarchy, unrestricted gun rights, and secession.

name: Pim Fortuyn
description: Dutch sociologist and politician, founder of the LPF assassinated in 2002. Openly gay, he combined secularism, LGBT rights, and euthanasia with fierce opposition to multiculturalism and Islamic immigration, free-market deregulation, direct democracy, and Euroscepticism.

name: Klaus Schwab
description: German economist and engineer, founder of the World Economic Forum in Davos (1971–2025). He theorized stakeholder capitalism, the Fourth Industrial Revolution, and the Great Reset, proposing public-private global governance, ESG goals, decarbonization, and biodigital convergence.

name: Subcomandante Marcos
description: Spokesperson and strategist of the Zapatista Army of National Liberation (EZLN) in Chiapas since the 1994 uprising. He fused Marxism and Mayan cosmology into Neozapatismo, advocating communal self-government ('commanding by obeying'), anti-capitalism, and alter-globalization.

name: Michael Collins
description: Irish revolutionary leader and statesman, IRA Director of Intelligence and Minister for Finance in the War of Independence. He negotiated the 1921 Anglo-Irish Treaty, chaired the Irish Free State, and advocated economic modernization and the Gaelic cultural revival.

name: José Gervasio Artigas
description: Leader of the Oriental Revolution and Protector of the Free Peoples (1815–1820). In the Instructions of the Year XIII and the 1815 Land Regulation, he advocated republican confederalism against Buenos Aires centralism, civil and religious liberty, and popular agrarian reform.

name: Costin Vlad Alamariu (BAP)
description: Romanian-American political philosopher and author writing under the pseudonym Bronze Age Pervert, advocating Nietzschean aristocratic vitalism, classical Bronze Age heroism, eugenics, and fierce opposition to modern liberal egalitarianism.

name: Campos Sales
description: President of Brazil (1898–1902) and a São Paulo republican, he created the 'politics of the governors', trading federal support for the loyalty of state oligarchies, and restored finances with the funding loan, spending cuts and higher taxes.

name: Floriano Peixoto
description: Marshal and second president of Brazil (1891–1894), the 'Iron Marshal' consolidated the Republic by force against the Armada Revolt and the Federalist Revolution, with Jacobin nationalism, states of siege and centralization.

name: Henri Bergson
description: French philosopher and Nobel laureate in Literature (1927), he formulated the élan vital and creative duration against mechanism, defending intuition, creative evolution and an open morality, and backed the League of Nations and the Allies.

name: René Guénon
description: French metaphysician who converted to Sufism in Cairo and founded perennialist Traditionalism, he condemns the modern world, egalitarianism and democracy in the name of primordial Tradition, initiatic hierarchy and esotericism.

name: Abelardo de la Espriella
description: President of Colombia since 2026 and a lawyer by profession. He takes a hard line against armed groups, ending peace talks with them, and wants to shrink the state and deregulate the economy. A conservative Catholic, he opposes abortion.

name: Antonio Negri
description: Italian philosopher of operaismo and autonomism, co-author of Empire, who sees the global multitude as the subject of revolution. He defends the commons against capital and the state, and was jailed in the 1970s.

name: Francis Fukuyama
description: American political scientist, author of The End of History, who argues that liberal democracy and the market have prevailed. He broke with the neoconservatives after the Iraq War and defends a strong, capable state.

name: Giuseppe Garibaldi
description: Italian general and hero of unification who fought with the Red Shirts and in South America. A republican, nationalist, anticlerical and volunteerist, he later accepted the Savoy monarchy for the sake of Italian unity.

name: Amadeo Bordiga
description: Founder of the Communist Party of Italy and theorist of the communist left, he rejected democracy, parliamentarism and Stalinism. He defended a centralized vanguard party and the abolition of the market, wages and commodities.

name: Oscar Wilde
description: Irish writer and leading aesthete, jailed for homosexuality in 1895. In The Soul of Man under Socialism he proposes a libertarian socialism that frees the individual from property and authority.

name: H. G. Wells
description: British science fiction writer and Fabian socialist who advocated scientific planning, universal education and a world government to prevent war. He criticized imperialism and institutional religion.

name: Bertrand Russell
description: British philosopher and logician, an atheist and pacifist, jailed for opposing the First World War. He defended democratic socialism, individual liberties, secularism and nuclear disarmament, while criticizing Soviet communism.

name: Herbert Marcuse
description: German-American Frankfurt School philosopher and a reference of the 1968 New Left. In One-Dimensional Man he criticizes the consumerism and technocracy of advanced capitalism and defends sexual liberation and radical refusal.

name: Nigel Farage
description: British politician, leader of Reform UK and a central figure of Brexit. He defends national sovereignty, mass deportations, scrapping net zero targets and tax cuts, and is closely aligned with Donald Trump.

name: Andrew Jackson
description: Seventh US president (1829–1837), a populist general and founder of the Democratic Party. He fought the Bank of the United States, championed the white common man and expansion, forced the removal of Native Americans and owned slaves.

name: Ferdinand Marcos
description: President of the Philippines from 1965 to 1986, he imposed martial law in 1972 and ruled as a dictator. A US-allied anticommunist, he centralized power, persecuted the opposition and enriched himself through crony capitalism.

name: Bobby Fischer
description: American chess player and 1972 world champion who broke with the US and came to promote antisemitic conspiracy theories, Holocaust denial and support for the 9/11 attacks. He lived his last years in exile in Iceland.

name: Leonid Brezhnev
description: General Secretary of the Soviet Communist Party from 1964 to 1982, he led the USSR through the Stagnation era. He kept central planning and one-party rule, repressed dissidents, formulated the Brezhnev Doctrine, invaded Afghanistan and pursued détente with the US.

name: Juan Manuel Santos
description: President of Colombia (2010–2018) and Nobel Peace laureate. Defence minister during the offensive against the FARC, he later negotiated the 2016 peace deal with them, passed a land restitution law for victims and opened the economy, signing the OECD accession.

name: Zhuangzi
description: Chinese Daoist philosopher of the Warring States period and author of the Zhuangzi. He champions spontaneous freedom, relativism and a simple natural life, refuses public office and scorns conventional morality and the ambitions of the state.

name: Laozi
description: Chinese sage traditionally credited with the Dao De Jing and the founding of Daoism. He advocates wu wei, a ruler who barely governs, small peaceful states, a simple life and distrust of learning, weapons and luxury.

name: Mozi
description: Chinese philosopher and founder of Mohism who preaches impartial care for all, rulers chosen by merit, frugality and only defensive war, and sees the will of Heaven as the basis of morality and politics.

name: Spartacus
description: Thracian gladiator who led the largest slave revolt against Rome (73–71 BC). He raised an army of tens of thousands of enslaved people, defeated Roman legions and shared the plunder equally until Crassus crushed it.

name: Tiberius Gracchus
description: Roman tribune of the plebs who proposed the 133 BC agrarian law, capping the public land held by the rich and giving it to the poor. He bypassed the Senate, appealed to the popular assembly and was killed by senators.

name: Gaius Gracchus
description: Roman tribune of the plebs and brother of Tiberius, he passed subsidized grain sales, colonies, public works and court reform and proposed citizenship for the Latins. Hunted by the Senate, he died in 121 BC.

name: Mazdak
description: Persian reformer of the Sasanian era who preached sharing of goods, an end to concentrated wealth and nonviolence. Backed by King Kavad I, he opened granaries in a famine but was massacred with his followers around 524.

name: John Ball
description: English priest who preached equality ("When Adam delved and Eve span, who was then the gentleman?") and an end to serfdom, nobility and the church hierarchy. He was the voice of the 1381 Peasants' Revolt and was executed.

name: Wat Tyler
description: Leader of the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381. He demanded an end to serfdom, low rents, free trade and the seizure of church property, always loyal to King Richard II; he was killed by an official at Smithfield.

name: Gerrard Winstanley
description: 17th-century Englishman, leader of the Diggers and author of The Law of Freedom, who defended common land, an end to private land and wage labor, a republic and nonviolence, in a Christian and rationalist key.

name: Jean Meslier
description: French priest who secretly wrote an atheist and communist Testament, attacking religion, monarchy, nobility and property and defending egalitarian parish communes. It was published only after his death.

name: Étienne de La Boétie
description: French magistrate and humanist, author of the Discourse on Voluntary Servitude, which argues that tyranny survives only because people consent to it. He proposes peaceful refusal to obey, not violence, as the path to freedom.

name: William Godwin
description: English philosopher and author of Political Justice, regarded as the father of philosophical anarchism. He defends abolishing government and unequal property, reason as the guide, education and nonviolence, and also criticizes marriage.

name: Thomas Spence
