description: English reformer who proposed that land belong to parishes, with rents paid into local funds financing services and an income for all. Jailed repeatedly for his radical pamphlets, he defended democracy.

name: Nestor Makhno
description: Ukrainian anarchist who led the Revolutionary Insurgent Army of Ukraine (1918–1921) against Germans, Whites and Reds. He defended free communes, soviets and peasant self-management in the Free Territory until the Bolsheviks crushed it; he died in exile in Paris.

name: Élisée Reclus
description: French geographer and anarchist, a Communard and author of the Universal Geography and Man and the Earth. He defends anarcho-communism, abolishing the state and property, vegetarianism, equality among peoples and harmony with nature.

name: Gary Johnson
description: Former Republican governor of New Mexico (1995–2003) and Libertarian presidential candidate in 2012 and 2016. He defends cutting spending and taxes, legalizing marijuana, a balanced budget, free trade, more open immigration and less military intervention.

name: Chase Oliver
description: Politician and 2024 Libertarian Party presidential candidate. He defends legalizing drugs, closing overseas bases, leaving NATO, ending military aid to Israel and Ukraine, open immigration reform, abortion rights, lower taxes and civil liberties.

name: João Amoêdo
description: Banker, founder of the Novo Party and 2018 presidential candidate in Brazil. Economically liberal and socially conservative, he defends privatizing Petrobras and public banks, a leaner state and pension reform, and favors gun ownership while opposing drugs and abortion.

name: Jackson Hinkle
description: American commentator and co-founder of the American Communist Party (2024). A self-described Marxist-Leninist who calls himself a Christian patriot, he defends Palestine, Putin's Russia and an end to US intervention abroad, and has been linked to the label "MAGA communism".

name: Zakhar Prilepin
description: Russian writer and politician, former leader of the For Truth party and co-chair of A Just Russia until 2025. A left-wing nationalist with National Bolshevik roots, he backs Putin and the war in Ukraine, fought in the Donbas and defends a strong, social and imperial state.

name: Jordan Bardella
description: President of the National Rally since 2022 and an MEP. He defends cutting immigration, national preference in benefits, law and order, sovereignty against the EU and tax cuts on energy, but backs sending weapons to Ukraine.

name: Santiago Abascal
description: President of Vox since 2014 and a deputy for Madrid. He defends Spain's unity and an end to the autonomous regions, remigration and deportations, national priority, the traditional family, and opposes abortion, gender and climate agendas and high taxes.

name: Gatis Lagzdiņš (Sv3rige)
description: Latvian YouTuber who advocates eating raw meat, flat Earth theory and opposition to veganism, with protests at vegan festivals, such as the 2019 London one that got him fined.

name: Aajonus Vonderplanitz
description: American alternative nutritionist who advocated the Primal Diet of raw meat, eggs and dairy and founded Right to Choose Healthy Food for the right to raw milk, opposing the FDA, vaccines and conventional medicine.

name: Raphael Machado
description: A lawyer trained at UFRJ and founder of Nova Resistência (2015), he spreads Dugin's Fourth Political Theory in Brazil: multipolarity, anti-Americanism, Vargas-style labor politics and Ibero-American integration.

name: Mark Rutte
description: NATO Secretary General since 2024 and prime minister of the Netherlands for 14 years (2010–2024), leader of the VVD. A liberal conservative, he defends free markets, fiscal discipline, tighter asylum, support for Ukraine and 5% of GDP on defense.

name: Johannes Kaiser
description: Chilean politician, activist and YouTuber, a deputy from 2022 to 2026 and founder of the National Libertarian Party. A paleolibertarian and reactionary, he defends a minimal state, free markets, hard immigration control, traditional values and Pinochet's legacy.

name: Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan
description: Emir of Abu Dhabi (1966–2004) and first president of the United Arab Emirates, which he unified in 1971. An absolute, paternalistic monarch, he redistributed oil wealth, favoured mediation and foreign aid, and kept Islam as the basis of the state.

name: Carlos Drummond de Andrade
description: Poet and chief of staff to the education minister under Vargas's authoritarian Estado Novo, later a newspaper columnist. A left-wing humanist, he wrote for a communist daily and published A Rosa do Povo (1945), poetry against war and oppression.

name: Graciliano Ramos
description: Novelist and former small-town mayor, jailed without trial by the Vargas regime in 1936, which inspired Memórias do Cárcere. An atheist, he joined the Brazilian Communist Party in 1945 and portrayed the misery of the northeastern backlands in Barren Lives.

name: Euclides da Cunha
description: Military engineer, republican and positivist, he covered the Canudos War for a São Paulo newspaper and wrote Rebellion in the Backlands, which condemns the massacre of the rural settlers. He later denounced the exploitation of Amazon rubber tappers.

name: Necmettin Erbakan
description: Turkish engineer and professor, founder of the Islamist Milli Görüş movement and prime minister (1996–97) until the military forced him out. He advocated an interest-free Just Order, domestic heavy industry and economic integration of Muslim countries (D-8).

name: Péter Magyar
description: Lawyer and former Fidesz insider who broke with Orbán in 2024 and led Tisza to victory in 2026, becoming Hungary's prime minister. He promises rule of law, anti-corruption and alignment with the EU and NATO, while keeping a hard line on migration.

name: Suharto
description: Indonesian general who ruled the so-called New Order from 1967 to 1998, with the army at the center of the state, an official party (Golkar), anticommunism (the 1965–66 massacres), liberal technocrats and rapid growth, but also corruption and repression.

name: Hayato Ikeda
description: Japanese prime minister from 1960 to 1964, a former Finance Ministry bureaucrat who replaced the debate over the US treaty with the Income Doubling Plan and led Japan to the peak of its economic miracle and the Tokyo Olympics.

name: Shigeru Yoshida
description: Japanese diplomat and prime minister (1946–47, 1948–54) who rebuilt the country under the American occupation, accepted the pacifist Constitution, signed the San Francisco Treaty and set the Yoshida Doctrine: security with the US, effort on the economy.

name: Oscar Niemeyer
description: Brazilian architect who designed the buildings of Brasília at Kubitschek's invitation and took curved modernism to the world, always a Communist Party militant and critic of inequality, which cost him exile under the dictatorship.

name: Chiang Ching-kuo
description: Son of Chiang Kai-shek, trained in the Soviet Union, he headed the Kuomintang's political police, served as premier and president of Taiwan (1978–88), carried out the Ten Major Construction Projects and, late in life, lifted martial law and opened the democratic transition.

name: Raúl Prebisch
description: An Argentine economist, Prebisch created the center–periphery thesis and led ECLAC and UNCTAD, advocating industrialization and regional integration so Latin America could escape deteriorating terms of trade.

name: Michał Kalecki
description: A Polish Marxist economist, Kalecki anticipated Keynes's theory of effective demand, analyzed the political business cycle of full employment, and worked in socialist Poland's planning while protesting the antisemitic purge of 1968.

name: Dmitry Medvedev
description: President of Russia (2008–2012) and Putin's prime minister, Medvedev, who pitched himself as a technological modernizer, turned hawk: deputy chairman of the Security Council, he threatens nuclear weapons and defends the war in Ukraine.

name: Giovanni Gentile
description: An idealist philosopher of actualism, Gentile was Mussolini's education minister, reformed Italian schooling, wrote the Manifesto of Fascist Intellectuals and fascism's doctrinal core, and was killed by partisans in 1944.

name: Itamar Franco
description: A politician from Minas Gerais, Itamar took the presidency after Collor's impeachment (1992–94), launched the Real Plan, defended a strong state in the economy and, as state governor, declared a moratorium on his state's debt to the federal government.

name: Fernando Collor
description: Elected president (1990–92) as a "hunter of maharajas" against inflated public salaries, Collor froze savings accounts in his stabilization plan, opened the economy and began privatizations; he resigned facing impeachment and, as senator, was convicted of corruption in 2023.

name: Júlio Prestes
description: A politician of São Paulo's Republican Party and governor of São Paulo (1927–30), Júlio Prestes won the 1930 presidential election under the coffee-and-milk oligarchic pact, but was barred from taking office by the 1930 Revolution.

name: João Figueiredo
description: A general and the last president of the military dictatorship (1979–85), Figueiredo signed the Amnesty Law and led a controlled opening, but kept up repression, rejected the direct-elections campaign and faced the foreign debt crisis.

name: John Adams
description: A founder and the second president of the United States, Adams led the Federalists, defended a mixed government with a strong executive and an elite Senate, avoided war with France and signed the Alien and Sedition Acts.

name: James Monroe
description: The fifth president of the United States, Monroe presided over the Era of Good Feelings, proclaimed the Monroe Doctrine against European recolonization of the Americas, bought Florida and signed the Missouri Compromise, upholding slavery.

name: Allan Kardec
description: A French educator, Kardec codified Spiritism in The Spirits' Book (1857): God, reincarnation and moral evolution, charity above dogma and no clergy, reconciling science and faith while staying out of party politics.

name: Bezerra de Menezes
description: A physician and liberal politician of the Brazilian Empire, a city councillor and deputy known as the "Doctor of the Poor", he embraced Spiritism in 1886 and presided over the Brazilian Spiritist Federation, making charity and Kardec's doctrine its foundation in Brazil.

name: Miguel Primo de Rivera
description: General and dictator of Spain from 1923 to 1930, Marquis of Estella: backed by Alfonso XIII, he suspended the Constitution, created the Patriotic Union and ruled through censorship, public works, corporatism and repression of Catalanism.

name: Elias Jabbour
description: UERJ economist and geographer, PCdoB leader and author of China: Socialism of the 21st Century; he defends market socialism, a project-based economy with the state as chief entrepreneur, and a China-led multipolar world.

name: Ted Cruz
description: Republican senator from Texas since 2013 and 2016 presidential candidate, a constitutional lawyer and evangelical Christian. He defends tax cuts, free trade, border control, firm support for Israel and a hard line on Iran and China.

name: Ben Sasse
description: Historian and former Republican senator from Nebraska (2015–2023), later president of the University of Florida. A critic of Trump populism, he defends free markets, federalism, entitlement reform, support for Ukraine and a hard line on China and Russia.

name: Pete Hegseth
description: Army veteran and former Fox News host, he has led the Pentagon (renamed Department of War) since 2025. He defends a warrior ethos, cuts to diversity programs, a ban on transgender troops, Christian nationalism and military action against cartels.

name: Rand Paul
description: Ophthalmologist and Republican senator from Kentucky since 2011, son of Ron Paul. A conservative libertarian, he defends minimal government, spending cuts, ending the president's tariff power, non-intervention and limits on surveillance; opposes abortion.

name: Heinrich Himmler
description: Reichsführer-SS, Himmler headed the SS, the Gestapo and the German police, organized the concentration and extermination camps and carried out the Holocaust, along with Germanization projects and racial mysticism. He killed himself on capture in 1945.

name: Alexander Rüstow
description: German sociologist and economist, Rüstow popularized the term neoliberalism at the 1938 Walter Lippmann Colloquium and defended a vital liberalism: a strong state against monopolies, social policy and a critique of laissez-faire. He lived in exile in Turkey during Nazism.

name: Alfred Müller-Armack
description: Economist and Erhard's state secretary, Müller-Armack coined the term social market economy in 1946 and shaped it as a synthesis of free markets and social policy, the basis of the German economic miracle. He also championed European integration.

name: Walter Eucken
description: German economist of the Freiburg School and an opponent of Nazism, Eucken founded ordoliberalism: he defended a competitive order guaranteed by a strong state, against monopolies, cartels and central planning. He inspired the German social market economy.

name: John A. Macdonald
description: Canada's first prime minister, a Conservative and architect of the 1867 Confederation: he built the transcontinental railway, adopted the protectionist National Policy tariffs, crushed the Métis Rebellion and created the Indigenous residential schools.

name: Pierre Poilievre
description: Leader of the Conservative Party since 2022: he vows to cut taxes and the carbon tax, tie immigration to housing supply, toughen sentences, defund the CBC and back pipelines and bitcoin, in a populist message against the elites.

name: Benito Juárez
description: Liberal president of Mexico (1858–1872) of Zapotec origin: he led the Reform, which separated church and state and seized clerical property, resisted the French intervention, had Maximilian shot and governed with emergency powers.

name: Porfirio Díaz
description: Dictator-president of Mexico for about 30 years (1876–1911): he imposed "order and progress" through rural police and repression, drew in foreign capital, railways and large estates, made peace with the Church and fell to the Mexican Revolution.

name: Andrés Manuel López Obrador
description: President of Mexico (2018–2024) for Morena: a left-wing nationalism that strengthened Pemex and CFE, expanded pensions and welfare programs, put public security in the Army's hands, attacked autonomous agencies and approved popular election of judges.

name: Robert Menzies
description: Prime minister of Australia (1939–1941, 1949–1966) and founder of the Liberal Party: an Anglophile monarchist and anti-communist (he tried to ban the Communist Party), sent troops to Korea and Vietnam and kept the White Australia policy.

name: John Howard
description: Conservative prime minister of Australia (1996–2007): he restricted guns after Port Arthur, introduced the GST, privatised Telstra, deregulated labour, hardened immigration and sent troops to Iraq and Afghanistan.

name: Roger Douglas
description: New Zealand Finance Minister (1984–88) in the Lange Labour government, he devised Rogernomics: a floating dollar, privatisations, the end of subsidies and a consumption tax. He later co-founded the liberal ACT party.

name: Fethullah Gülen
description: Turkish preacher and theologian, leader of the Hizmet movement: he promoted education, science, interfaith dialogue and Islam in public life, condemning the politicization of religion. Exiled in the US since 1999, he denied Ankara's charge of ordering the 2016 coup.

name: Osama bin Laden
description: Saudi founder of al-Qaeda: he financed the anti-Soviet jihad in Afghanistan, declared war on the US in 1996 over its military presence in Saudi Arabia, and sought a caliphate under sharia. He planned the 9/11 attacks and was killed in Pakistan in 2011.
